column2: Doctor of Business Administration in Finance
column16:
Submit an online application
Upload a professional resumé
Submit a 750-1,000 word statement of purpose describing your professional goals and aspirations, your previous academic preparation, and an explanation of how the DBA program fits your professional and personal aspirations.
Submit two letters of recommendation. At least one of the letters must come from a faculty member or other individual qualified to attest to your academic ability. You will submit contact information for the recommenders in the online application and they will receive instructions for submitting their letters electronically.
Submit official transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended.
An earned master’s degree in business or a related field from a regionally accredited institution, or its international equivalent, with a minimum GPA of 3.0
An earned bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution, or its international equivalent, with a minimum GPA of 3.0
Students whose native language is not English must submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores unless they have earned a degree from an accredited United States institution or from an institution in a country where English is the official language. Minimum scores required for TOEFL are 80 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based), or 550 (paper-based). The minimum IELTS score is 6.5.
Students are not required to submit GRE or GMAT scores.
column47: The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) program at Sacred Heart University’s Jack Welch College of Business & Technology is a practitioner-oriented doctoral program designed for executives who seek to further their careers as transformational leaders, applied researchers, and university faculty. Rooted in applied research, the program allows students to delve into real-world business challenges, integrating academic theories with practical solutions. Our DBA curriculum is designed to sharpen critical thinking, analytical skills, and leadership capabilities, preparing graduates to influence decision-making at the highest levels of organizations. The program emphasizes ethical leadership and social responsibility, aligning with Sacred Heart University's mission. Graduates emerge as thought leaders, equipped to contribute to both academic scholarship and professional practice, making a significant impact in their chosen fields.
column50: AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business) accreditation for the Jack Welch College of Business & Technology

column2: Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership
column16:
Admission to the Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership program is a competitive process. Admission is based upon an applicant's academic record, professional experience, recommendations, and a personal interview with the Doctoral Admissions Committee.
Admission to the Ed.D. program requires:
*   An earned master's degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3.
*   Evidence of five or more years of professional experience in an educational leadership role (i.e., teacher, administrator, school leader, or other leadership role).
*   Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work submitted directly to Sacred Heart University.
*   Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's leadership potential and/or academic ability.
*   A written statement outlining the applicant's professional goals and interest in the Ed.D. program.
*   A current resume or curriculum vitae.
*   A successful interview with the Doctoral Admissions Committee.
*   Submission of the completed online application and application fee.
column38: College of Education and Human Development
column47: The Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Educational Leadership program, developed and taught by accomplished practitioner-scholars, prepares educational leaders for roles in both public and private schools, higher education, and other educational and nonprofit settings. The program is committed to developing leaders who can translate current research and best practices into effective action. Designed for working professionals, the program offers flexible scheduling through a blended model of online and face-to-face instruction at our Fairfield campus. Graduates of the Ed.D. program serve as leaders, scholars, and advocates for equity and excellence. Through a focus on collaboration and social justice, graduates are equipped with a diverse set of professional skills including: research and evaluation, program and policy development, advocacy, communication, and management.

column2: Doctor of Education in Higher Education Leadership
column16:
A master's degree in a related field from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA
Official transcripts from all institutions attended
Two letters of recommendation (professional or academic)
Current resume
Statement of professional goals and objectives
No GRE required
column47: Our Doctor of Education (EdD) in Higher Education Leadership program is ideal for professionals seeking to advance into leadership and management positions in colleges and universities. The curriculum emphasizes leadership, organizational behavior, policy, finance, and assessment in higher education settings. With an EdD, you’ll become a critical analyst of higher education policy and practice, capable of leading institutions through complex changes. This program is designed for working professionals, with flexible evening and weekend classes offered at our Stamford graduate center. As an EdD in Higher Education Leadership student, you will delve into crucial topics relevant to today's evolving higher education landscape. This program is designed to provide you with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills needed to address complex challenges in higher education. You'll learn about: Leadership and Organizational Change (understanding theories of leadership, organizational behavior, and change management within higher education institutions); Higher Education Policy and Governance (analyzing the policy landscape, governance structures, and legal frameworks impacting colleges and universities); Finance and Resource Management (exploring financial models, budgeting, and resource allocation strategies specific to higher education); Assessment and Accreditation (learning about institutional effectiveness, program evaluation, and the accreditation process); Research Methods and Data Analysis (developing advanced research skills, including qualitative and quantitative methodologies, to inform data-driven decision-making); Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (examining issues of access, equity, and inclusion in higher education and developing strategies for fostering inclusive environments); and Strategic Planning and Innovation (mastering the principles of strategic planning, innovation, and entrepreneurship in higher education).

column2: Doctor of Physical Therapy
column16: The Department of Physical Therapy participates in the Physical Therapy Centralized Application Service (PTCAS). All applicants must apply through PTCAS. Applicants are expected to possess a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants may be admitted to the DPT program with the understanding that the undergraduate degree will be completed prior to the start of the professional phase of the program. Minimum Cumulative GPA 3.0. Minimum Science GPA 2.75. The following must be submitted to PTCAS: Completed online application to PTCAS. Official transcripts from ALL colleges and universities attended. Two letters of recommendation from professional individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential, communication skills, and work ethic. One letter must be from a licensed physical therapist and one from a college professor. A minimum of 50 observation hours supervised by a licensed Physical Therapist. These hours can be paid or volunteer, in a minimum of two different settings. All applicants must submit official GRE scores directly from ETS to PTCAS (Sacred Heart University Code: 0746). The GRE must be taken within five years of the application. A CV or Resume is required from all applicants. A personal statement, one page in length, addressing the following: Why are you interested in pursuing a career in physical therapy? Why have you selected Sacred Heart University's DPT program? Additional requirements apply for international applicants, including TOEFL scores, WES evaluation, and financial certification.
column47: The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program at Sacred Heart University is a rigorous, post-baccalaureate, entry-level professional program designed to prepare students for the practice of physical therapy. The DPT program is a full-time, three-year program consisting of a sequential plan of study that includes classroom, laboratory, and clinical coursework. The program is specifically designed to meet the academic and clinical requirements for students to be eligible for licensure examinations in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Physical therapists are health care professionals who help patients reduce pain and improve or restore mobility. They treat patients of all ages who have injuries, disabilities, or other health conditions. The comprehensive program prepares students as generalist physical therapy practitioners, while emphasizing a commitment to community service, global engagement, and professional development. The curriculum integrates basic sciences, clinical sciences, and research to prepare graduates for contemporary physical therapy practice. The program’s learning environment stresses critical thinking, problem-solving, and evidence-based practice across the lifespan. The Doctor of Physical Therapy program at Sacred Heart University is committed to providing outstanding education, compassionate service, and rigorous scholarship within an interprofessional environment dedicated to improving health outcomes.
column50: The Doctor of Physical Therapy program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org. If needing to contact the program/institution directly, please call 203-371-7788 or email dpt@sacredheart.edu. The program is undergoing a review for re-accreditation that will conclude in 2023.

column2: Family Nurse Practitioner Doctor of Nursing Practice
column16: Master of Science in Nursing from an accredited institution. Minimum GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Current, unencumbered RN license from the state in which the student plans to complete clinical hours. Current national certification as an Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN). Evidence of successful completion of a graduate-level statistics course. Two letters of recommendation from professional colleagues/supervisors who can attest to the applicant’s academic and clinical abilities. Current curriculum vitae or résumé. Statement of professional goals. Interview with a faculty member.
column47: The DNP is a terminal practice degree that prepares advanced practice nurses for leadership roles in healthcare. Sacred Heart University offers a DNP with several concentrations. The program is designed to prepare graduates to translate research into practice, lead quality improvement initiatives, and impact healthcare policy. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practice, patient safety, health informatics, and interprofessional collaboration. Students will engage in scholarly activities, including the completion of a DNP project, which addresses a clinical problem or health system issue. The DNP program is offered in both full-time and part-time formats. The Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) concentration within the DNP program prepares registered nurses to provide comprehensive primary healthcare to individuals and and families across the lifespan. FNPs assess, diagnose, treat, and manage acute and chronic illnesses, focusing on health promotion, disease prevention, and patient education. Graduates are eligible for national certification as a Family Nurse Practitioner and state licensure.
column50: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE), 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.

column2: Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness
column16:
Applicants for admission to the Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness program must possess a master's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following materials:
*   Online application
*   Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework
*   Current resume or curriculum vitae
*   Three letters of recommendation submitted by former professors or supervisors
*   A personal statement of at least 750 words describing professional experiences, reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in ODCE, and career aspirations following completion of the degree
*   A research statement of 500 words or less addressing a current issue in organization development, change, or effectiveness. The statement should articulate a research question that could be explored in the Ph.D. program.
*   Official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) or Graduate Management Admissions Test (GMAT) must be submitted unless the applicant has received a master’s degree from Sacred Heart University and maintained a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. The GRE/GMAT must have been taken within the last five years.
*   All international students from non-English speaking countries must submit official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
column47: Sacred Heart University’s Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness (ODCE) prepares leaders to transform organizations and communities through theory and practice. The doctoral program prepares scholar-practitioners who apply critical inquiry, ethical decision-making, and organizational theory to design and implement transformational change. Students develop knowledge and skills to lead complex change processes, evaluate organizational interventions, and contribute to the body of knowledge in ODCE. This program is for working professionals with a minimum of a master’s degree and at least five years of professional work experience. Students are prepared for careers in internal and external consulting, human resources, organizational leadership, and academia. The ODCE Ph.D. is a cohort model where students work together from admission to graduation and develop professional networks and friendships. Courses are delivered in a hybrid format, with monthly residencies meeting in person on the Sacred Heart University campus. Students complete their studies with a research-based dissertation.

column2: Ph.D. in Social Work
column16: The Social Work Ph.D. program will accept applications on a rolling basis. Admission requires a master’s degree in social work from a CSWE-accredited program, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). The following documents must be submitted to complete your application: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended; Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to your academic abilities and readiness for doctoral study. At least one of these letters must be from an academic source; Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV); Personal statement detailing your academic and professional goals, research interests, and why you are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. in Social Work at Sacred Heart University (minimum 750 words); Master’s degree writing sample (e.g., thesis, research paper, scholarly paper, journal article, etc.) that demonstrates your capacity for scholarly writing; Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required; A copy of your current social work license (LCSW preferred); Non-native English speakers must submit a Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) score. A minimum TOEFL score of 80 (internet-based) or IELTS score of 6.5 is required.
column47: Our online Ph.D. in Social Work program is designed for social work professionals who want to develop the advanced research and practice skills needed to make a meaningful impact in the field. This unique program provides an opportunity for students to advance their knowledge and prepare for leadership roles in social work education, administration, practice, and research. With a focus on social justice and human rights, students in our Ph.D. in Social Work program engage in rigorous scholarship, critical thinking, and ethical decision-making. Through advanced coursework, research projects, and dissertation, students will gain the expertise to address complex social problems and contribute to the advancement of social work knowledge. The curriculum is delivered in an online, interactive format, allowing working professionals to balance their studies with their personal and professional commitments.

column2: Post-Master's Doctor of Nursing Practice
column16:
Completed online graduate application (including the non-refundable application fee)
Official transcripts of all college-level work (undergraduate and graduate) sent directly from the issuing institution(s). If accepted, official final transcripts noting degree conferral are required prior to matriculation.
Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Official transcripts verifying a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) degree with an overall GPA of 3.25 on a 4.0 scale from a nationally accredited program. The Post-Master's DNP requires a non-clinical MSN.
Current, active, unencumbered RN license(s) from the state(s) in which clinical practice will occur and current, active, unencumbered advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) license(s), if applicable.
Professional Resume or Curriculum Vitae
Personal Statement/Essay that speaks to your professional goals and how the DNP will help you achieve them (1-2 pages)
Two letters of recommendation (one from a supervisor/employer and one from an academician is preferred)
Interview with a College of Nursing faculty member
Evidence of completed 500 clinical hours at the graduate level
Copy of BLS/ACLS/PALS certification(s) per specialty
column47:
The Post-Master’s DNP is designed for master’s-prepared advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) seeking to advance their knowledge and skills in evidence-based practice, leadership, and health care policy. It is a doctoral-level program to prepare the APRN at the highest level of clinical nursing practice. The program focuses on providing advanced knowledge in nursing science, theory, and research, as well as developing advanced competencies in evidence-based practice, organizational leadership, and health care systems. Graduates of the program are prepared to lead complex health care systems, translate research into practice, and improve population health outcomes. Coursework for the DNP program builds upon master’s level coursework in the areas of: Nurse Anesthesia, Family Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Leader.
The DNP curriculum is based on the AACN’s Essentials of Doctoral Education for Advanced Practice.
For more information, please visit the Sacred Heart University College of Nursing website.
column50: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) program is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

column2: Master of Science in Athletic Training
column16: Baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution, or international equivalent. Undergraduate cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Completion of prerequisite coursework (Anatomy and Physiology I with lab, Anatomy and Physiology II with lab, Biology with lab, Chemistry with lab, Physics with lab, Statistics, General Psychology, and Medical Terminology). Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Two letters of recommendation from faculty members, supervisors, or athletic training professionals. Resume or curriculum vitae. Personal statement addressing the applicant’s interest in the athletic training profession and desire to attend Sacred Heart University. Official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test are NOT required. Demonstration of 50 hours of observation under the direct supervision of a BOC-certified athletic trainer. The observation hours can be in any setting (e.g., high school, college/university, clinic, professional sport, industrial). These hours must be verified by the supervising athletic trainer(s). International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency through official TOEFL or IELTS scores unless they have completed a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution where English is the language of instruction. Official scores must be submitted directly to the Sacred Heart University Office of Graduate Admissions.
column47: The Sacred Heart University Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) is an entry-level professional program designed for students with a bachelor’s degree in a related field who are seeking to become certified athletic trainers. The program prepares students to become highly competent, compassionate, and ethical healthcare professionals capable of providing patient-centered care in a variety of clinical settings. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practice, critical thinking, and interprofessional collaboration, providing students with the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to excel in the dynamic field of athletic training.
column50: The Master of Science in Athletic Training program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE), 2001 K Street NW, Third Floor North, Washington, DC 20006. The program has been placed on Probation as of February 24, 2023, by the CAATE. For more information, please see the CAATE's Public Disclosure Statement.

column2: Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling
column16: To be considered for admission to the Sacred Heart University MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling program, you must hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution and a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. While a background in psychology or a related field is helpful, it is not required for admission. Candidates must provide: Completed Application Form, Resume, Personal Statement, Official Transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities, Two Letters of Recommendation, Interview.
column47: The CACREP-accredited online MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling program at Sacred Heart University prepares students for careers as licensed professional counselors (LPCs). In as few as three years, you can learn to assess, diagnose, and treat clients from diverse backgrounds in a wide variety of settings. Through comprehensive coursework, hands-on practicum and internship experiences, and faculty mentorship, you will develop the clinical skills and knowledge needed to help individuals, families, and groups achieve optimal mental health and well-being. Upon graduation, you will be eligible for licensure in many states, though requirements may vary by state. This program also fulfills the educational requirements for students interested in pursuing the Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT) credential.
column50: Accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP)

column2: Master of Arts in Film & Television Production
column16: Applicants for the Master of Arts in Film & Television Production are required to submit the following: A completed application, A non-refundable application fee, Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, including proof of bachelor's degree earned with an undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0. Two letters of recommendation from faculty or employers. A statement of purpose (500–1,000 words). A resume of professional and/or volunteer experience in the industry or other related fields. A writing sample of at least 5 pages, which can include creative writing (e.g., screenplay, short story, theatrical play) or analytical/critical writing (e.g., academic paper, critical essay, film analysis).
column47: The Master of Arts in Film & Television Production program is a cutting-edge, hands-on master’s degree designed for students who want to develop creative content for screens of all sizes, from web to television to theatrical release. In today’s rapidly evolving media landscape, the roles of writer, producer, director, and editor are often combined. Our program emphasizes storytelling across all platforms and provides students with skills in critical analysis, visual storytelling, writing for the screen, producing, directing, cinematography, editing, and post-production. The program offers students the opportunity to choose between a thesis or a capstone project. Upon completion, students will have a portfolio of work ready for the job market. Full-time and part-time options are available. The program can be completed in two years of full-time study.

column2: Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs
column16: All applicants for the Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and meet the general requirements for admission to graduate studies at Sacred Heart University. In addition, applicants for the Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs must submit the following: Official transcripts of all previous college work. There are no specific prerequisite courses required for admission to the program.
column38: College of Education and Human Development
column47: The Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs (MA-HESA) program at Sacred Heart University prepares students to serve in administrative and leadership roles within higher education settings. Students are trained to work effectively with diverse college students in areas such as student activities, residential life, career development, student leadership, admissions, and advising. This 36-credit program prepares students to become reflective practitioners by integrating theory, research, and practice in their chosen professional areas. The program emphasizes self-reflection, social justice, inclusion, ethical practices, and the development of effective leadership skills. Through classroom learning, fieldwork, and internships, students are prepared to be collaborative and innovative leaders and managers in higher education. The program is offered in a hybrid format.

column2: Master of Arts in Sports Communication and Media
column16: Completed online graduate application: A non-refundable application fee is required. The fee is waived for Sacred Heart University alumni. Official transcripts: From all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Applicants with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0 may be considered for conditional admission. Two letters of recommendation: From supervisors, professors, or others who can speak to the applicant’s professional or academic capabilities. (Required) Graduate Record Examination (GRE): The GRE is not required for admission. (Not Required) International applicants: Additional requirements include an official English translation of all academic records and official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS). A minimum TOEFL score of 80 (Internet-based) or IELTS score of 6.5 is required. International applicants must also provide evidence of adequate financial resources.
column47: The Master of Arts in Sports Communication & Media program at Sacred Heart University is a dynamic and innovative graduate program designed to equip students with the advanced knowledge and practical skills necessary to thrive in the rapidly evolving sports communication industry. This program provides an in-depth exploration of the theoretical, ethical, and strategic dimensions of sports media, preparing graduates for leadership roles in various facets of the field. The Mission of the Master of Arts in Sports Communication & Media program is to develop agile and ethically-minded professionals who possess a comprehensive understanding of the evolving sports communication landscape. Through a blend of theoretical foundations and practical applications, the program aims to cultivate critical thinking, effective communication, and media production skills, empowering graduates to create impactful narratives, manage complex communication challenges, and contribute meaningfully to the sports industry.

column2: Master of Arts in Strategic Communications and Public Relations
column47: The Sacred Heart University Master of Arts in Strategic Communication and Public Relations program provides a comprehensive graduate education for those seeking leadership roles in a wide range of communication fields. Through a curriculum that emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, students develop advanced skills in strategic planning, public relations, media relations, digital communication, crisis management, and persuasive messaging. The program is designed for current communication professionals seeking to advance their careers, as well as recent graduates looking to enter the dynamic world of strategic communication. Graduates emerge with a sophisticated understanding of the evolving media landscape and the ability to craft compelling narratives that resonate across diverse platforms. The program fosters critical thinking, ethical decision-making, and a global perspective essential for effective communication leadership in today's complex environment.

column2: Master of Arts in Teaching Music
column16: Admission to the M.A.T. program requires evidence of outstanding academic success and strong recommendations. Applicants must also complete the Sacred Heart University graduate application. Required documents include: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work completed. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale is required. Transcripts from outside the U.S. require a credential evaluation. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional work. Statement of purpose (500–1,000 words) describing the applicant’s interest in the field, career goals, and reasons for applying to the graduate program. A current résumé. Official GRE scores (if undergraduate GPA is below 3.0). Sacred Heart University's GRE code is 3780. Additional requirements for M.A.T. in Teaching Music: Audition and interview. A portfolio with recent examples of the applicant’s work may also be requested.
column47: The Master of Arts in Teaching (M.A.T.) is designed for college graduates who seek initial certification to teach at the elementary or secondary school levels. The M.A.T. program provides candidates with a solid theoretical and practical background in education. Through fieldwork and extensive clinical practice experiences, candidates learn to integrate theory and research with current best practices to become reflective practitioners who understand the diverse needs of students in public and private schools. The Music (PK-12) certification area is designed for individuals who hold an undergraduate degree in Music.
column50: The M.A.T. program in the Isabelle Farrington College of Education and Human Development has been awarded accreditation by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) for a period of seven years, from Fall 2021 to Fall 2028.

column2: Master of Business Administration
column16: Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 2.75. Required documents include official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities, a professional resume, two letters of recommendation, and a Statement of Purpose. International students must submit English proficiency test scores (TOEFL/IELTS). GMAT/GRE scores are recommended but not mandatory. Applicants need to complete an online application and pay the application fee.
column46: Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, Business Analytics
column47: The Sacred Heart University Master of Business Administration (MBA) program builds on your previous academic and professional experiences to transform you into an effective leader. With a strong emphasis on ethical decision-making, global awareness, and innovative problem-solving, the SHU MBA prepares you for success in today's dynamic business environment. Our rigorous curriculum, experienced faculty, and strong industry connections ensure you gain the knowledge, skills, and network needed to advance your career. The program offers a variety of specializations, including Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, and Business Analytics, allowing students to tailor their MBA to their career goals. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of international business practices and challenges and cultivate strong ethical decision-making skills crucial for responsible leadership.
column50: The Jack Welch College of Business & Technology at Sacred Heart University is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Film and Television Production
column47: The MFA in Film & Television at Sacred Heart University is an intensive, two-year, terminal degree program that trains students in the art and craft of visual storytelling. Students select a primary area of focus among the following: Producing, Directing, Screenwriting or Cinematography. The program emphasizes narrative fiction, creative collaboration, critical thinking, and independent filmmaking with a focus on preparing graduates for success in the entertainment industry. Students will receive extensive instruction in both theory and practice in the fields of film and television, with additional study in the critical, aesthetic, and historical aspects of these media. Throughout the program, students work in both individual and group settings to write, direct, and produce films of increasing complexity that culminate in a thesis film that meets professional standards. Students are given the opportunity to present their work at film festivals and industry showcases. Sacred Heart University’s MFA in Film & Television prepares graduates for careers as independent filmmakers, as well as for work in a variety of capacities in the professional film and television industries.

column2: Master of Health Administration
column16:
Minimum Requirements:
*   Possess a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution.
*   Demonstrate academic ability for graduate study as evidenced by your academic record.
*   Have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale).
*   Have completed undergraduate coursework in statistics and microeconomics or their equivalents (e.g., AP Economics, AP Statistics). If you have not taken these courses, you must successfully complete them by the time of enrollment.
*   Have at least two years of full-time post-baccalaureate experience in a health care setting or a related field (e.g., direct patient care, hospital administration, public health, health tech, health consulting, life sciences, biotech, pharma).
*   International applicants have additional requirements detailed on the International Applicants page.

Application Components:
*   Online Application
*   Transcripts
*   Letters of Recommendation (3 required)
*   Statement of Purpose (Required)
*   Resume or CV (Required)
*   Supplemental Questions (Required)
*   GRE (Optional)
*   TOEFL/IELTS (If applicable)
column47: The Master of Health Administration (MHA) program at Sacred Heart University is a 36-credit online or on-ground program designed for healthcare professionals seeking to advance their careers in leadership and management roles within the rapidly evolving healthcare industry. Our MHA program prepares you for executive-level positions in hospitals, health systems, long-term care facilities, consulting firms, pharmaceutical companies, and state and federal agencies. Upon completion of the MHA program, graduates will be able to: Master healthcare-specific management theories and practices; Exhibit leadership skills and competencies for various healthcare settings; Apply ethical principles to professional practice and decision-making; Analyze data and evidence for informed decision-making in healthcare administration; Articulate effective communication strategies for diverse healthcare stakeholders; Evaluate the impact of healthcare policy and regulations on organizations. Students will learn about: Healthcare Systems & Policy; Healthcare Finance; Strategic Management in Healthcare; Healthcare Law & Ethics; Quality Improvement in Healthcare; Health Informatics; Leadership in Healthcare Organizations; Research Methods in Health Administration.
column50: Sacred Heart University is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE).

column2: Master of Physician Assistant Studies
column16:
Admission to the Master of Physician Assistant Studies Program requires a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must apply to the PA Program through the Central Application Service for Physician Assistants (CASPA) at caspaonline.org. The application cycle opens in April annually. The deadline for CASPA application is September 1. It is recommended that applicants submit their applications early.

Minimum GPA requirements:
*   Cumulative GPA of 3.0
*   Science GPA of 3.0
*   A minimum of a “C” (2.0) is required for all prerequisite courses.

Prerequisite Courses (A minimum of “C” is required for all courses. All science courses must be for science majors.)

*   Biology with lab (2 semesters/8 credits)
*   Chemistry with lab (2 semesters/8 credits)
*   Anatomy & Physiology with lab (2 semesters/8 credits) (within 5 years of application)
*   Microbiology with lab (1 semester/4 credits)
*   Statistics (1 semester/3 credits)
*   Biochemistry or Organic Chemistry with lab (1 semester/4 credits)
*   Medical Terminology (1 semester/1 credit)

Other Admission Requirements:

*   Graduate Record Examination (GRE): General Test is required. The SHU code for the GRE is 3780.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation are required. Letters should be from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic preparedness, professional experience, and personal qualities for a career as a PA (e.g., professor, academic advisor, supervisor). It is recommended that at least one letter be from a practicing physician assistant or other healthcare provider with whom the applicant has worked directly.
*   Shadowing/Healthcare Experience: A minimum of 500 hours of direct patient care experience is required. Shadowing a PA is highly recommended.
*   International Applicants: Please refer to the Graduate International Admissions webpage for additional requirements.
*   Immunizations: All accepted applicants will be required to meet SHU's immunization requirements prior to matriculation. Details will be provided upon acceptance.
*   Background Check/Drug Screen: All accepted applicants will be required to successfully complete a criminal background check and drug screen prior to matriculation. Details will be provided upon acceptance.
*   Interview: Qualified applicants will be invited for an on-campus interview.
column47: The Master of Physician Assistant Studies (MPAS) Program at Sacred Heart University is an intensive 27-month, full-time program designed to prepare graduates to provide comprehensive health care services to diverse populations in a variety of clinical settings. The curriculum is delivered in a cohort model and designed to integrate a strong basic science foundation with clinical medicine. The program includes both didactic and supervised clinical practice experiences (SCPEs). Throughout the didactic year, students acquire the medical knowledge and clinical skills necessary to provide patient care within a medical team. During the clinical year, students participate in required and elective rotations designed to develop competence in primary care and medical and surgical specialties. The curriculum also emphasizes interprofessional collaboration, evidence-based medicine, patient advocacy, medical ethics, and cultural sensitivity to prepare students for the contemporary healthcare environment. Upon graduation, students are eligible to sit for the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), administered by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA). Completion of the program does not guarantee certification or state licensure.

column47: The Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics program at Sacred Heart University is designed for working professionals and recent graduates from a variety of backgrounds who want to make a difference in the healthcare field. In this program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to improve patient care outcomes and reduce costs using information technology and analytics. Healthcare informatics bridges the gap between clinical practice, information technology, and business, applying principles from all three to improve healthcare services and delivery. Our rigorous, relevant curriculum covers crucial topics in the field, including healthcare data analytics, project management, health information systems, health data security, and interoperability. Courses combine online learning with an intensive, immersive residency experience at the end of the program, which takes place on Sacred Heart's campus. Our faculty bring real-world experience to the classroom, ensuring that you graduate with practical, in-demand skills. Upon graduation, our program will prepare you to make an impact in a variety of healthcare settings. Learning Outcomes include: Analyze existing healthcare processes and identify opportunities for informatics interventions; Evaluate, design, and implement informatics solutions to improve patient outcomes, reduce costs, and enhance the efficiency of healthcare delivery; Lead and manage informatics projects, ensuring their successful integration into healthcare systems; Apply ethical and legal principles to the management and use of health information, ensuring patient privacy and data security; Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, bridging the gap between clinical, technical, and administrative teams; Utilize advanced data analytics techniques to interpret complex healthcare data and inform decision-making. Graduates of the MS in Healthcare Informatics program at Sacred Heart University are prepared for leadership roles in a variety of healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, government agencies, and technology companies. The Sacred Heart University Master of Science in Occupational Therapy program has a rich history of educating occupational therapists for more than 20 years, beginning as an entry-level master’s degree program, transitioning to a clinical doctoral program (OTD) in 2013 and now returning to the entry-level Master of Science degree (MSOT). The mission of the program is to educate competent and compassionate occupational therapists who are leaders, scholars, and innovators who serve the community through ethical and evidence-based practice across diverse settings. This mission is aligned with the vision of the University, College of Health Professions, and Department of Occupational Therapy.

The program is designed as a hybrid-model curriculum, integrating online coursework with face-to-face sessions and fieldwork experiences. This model allows for flexibility for the working student while ensuring a strong foundation in occupational therapy theory and practice. The curriculum emphasizes occupation-based, client-centered, and evidence-based practice to prepare graduates to work with individuals, groups, and populations across the lifespan in a variety of traditional and emerging practice settings. Students will engage in active learning through a variety of modalities, including case studies, simulations, projects, and collaborative discussions. The program culminates in a capstone experience where students apply their knowledge and skills to address a real-world occupational therapy challenge. Upon successful completion of the MSOT program, graduates will be eligible to sit for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) examination.
column50: The Master of Science in Occupational Therapy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA), located at 6116 Executive Boulevard, Suite 200, North Bethesda, MD 20852-4929. ACOTE’s telephone number c/o AOTA is (301) 652-AOTA and its Web address is www.acoteonline.org. Graduates of the program will be eligible to sit for the national certification examination for the Occupational Therapist administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). After successful completion of this exam, the individual will be an Occupational Therapist, Registered (OTR). In addition, all states require licensure in order to practice; however, state licenses are usually based on the results of the NBCOT Certification Examination. Note that a felony conviction may affect a graduate’s ability to sit for the NBCOT exam or to attain state licensure.

A master’s degree in Human Resource Management from Sacred Heart University prepares you to be a leader in the fast-paced, competitive world of business. Our Master of Science in Strategic Human Resource Management (MS in SHRM) emphasizes the strategic importance of human resources in organizations, and offers you a cutting-edge curriculum in organizational theory, data analytics, labor relations, employment law, talent acquisition, total rewards, and organizational development. Our program will provide you with the necessary skills and knowledge to address the contemporary challenges faced by global organizations today, helping you to lead their human resource function through data-driven decisions.

This means that students who graduate from the MS in SHRM program are fully prepared to take either the SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP certification exam.
The MS in SHRM can be completed on a full-time or part-time basis. Full-time students can complete the program in two years. Students have the option to pursue the degree completely online or in a hybrid format, which includes a blend of online and evening on-campus classes at our Fairfield, CT campus.
SHRM is the world's largest HR professional society. SHRM-certified professionals are recognized as experts and leaders in the HR field, and they are critical to the success of their organizations. Sacred Heart University's MS in SHRM prepares you to become an industry leader and to successfully obtain professional certification.

The program integrates data analysis, statistical modeling, and business intelligence to provide a comprehensive understanding of how data-driven insights can be leveraged for strategic advantage. The certificate is suitable for professionals seeking to enhance their analytical capabilities or those looking to pivot into data-centric roles within the business world.

column38: College of Health and Human Services
column47:
The Certificate of Advanced Study (CAS) in Play Therapy is designed for master’s level clinicians who seek to gain specialized knowledge and skills in play therapy. The CAS meets the educational requirements for the Registered Play Therapist™ (RPT™) and Supervisor (RPT-S™) credentials through the Association for Play Therapy (APT). The CAS is designed to facilitate the professional growth and development of students, preparing them to work effectively with children, adolescents, and families across diverse settings. The program also prepares clinicians for a variety of leadership positions within the field of play therapy.
Students completing the CAS in Play Therapy will be able to:
* Apply advanced knowledge of play therapy theories, techniques, and interventions to address the needs of diverse populations.
* Demonstrate ethical and culturally sensitive practice in play therapy, adhering to professional standards and guidelines.
* Integrate theoretical knowledge with practical skills to effectively assess, diagnose, and treat clients using play-based approaches.
* Utilize research and evidence-based practices to inform clinical decision-making in play therapy.
* Develop a strong professional identity as a play therapist, committed to lifelong learning and professional development.

column2: Sixth-Year Degree in SEAL for Social Justice Leadership

This program provides students with the opportunity to explore critical topics in educational leadership, social justice, and social-emotional learning. Graduates of the program will be prepared to assume leadership positions in various educational and community settings. Students will develop skills in the following areas: leading for social justice, fostering positive school cultures, creating inclusive learning environments, promoting social-emotional learning, implementing evidence-based practices, and advocating for equitable policies and practices. Through coursework, field experiences, and a capstone project, students will engage in deep inquiry into the challenges facing education and develop innovative solutions to promote social justice and equity. The program integrates the fields of educational leadership, social-emotional learning, and social justice. This combination offers a distinctive approach to preparing leaders who can drive positive change and create more inclusive and equitable educational systems.

The program will prepare educators to become leaders and innovators in STEAM education, capable of designing engaging and effective learning experiences for diverse student populations across different grade levels. Graduates will be equipped to teach STEAM in various educational settings, including K-12 schools, informal learning environments, and higher education. The program focuses on instructional strategies, curriculum development, and assessment methods specifically tailored to STEAM subjects. column47: The Sacred Heart University Coding Boot Camp is a non-credit certificate program designed to help students learn the skills necessary to become a full-stack developer in a hands-on, immersive learning environment. Students will gain practical experience with modern development tools and techniques, including HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, Bootstrap, Express.js, Node.js, React.js, Database Theory, MySQL, Command Line, Git, and Heroku. The program features challenging exercises, group projects, and portfolio development, preparing students for an entry-level position as a front-end or back-end web developer or to launch their own entrepreneurial venture. The program requires 24 weeks of part-time study or 12 weeks of full-time study and is delivered in a remote, synchronous format. column47: Sacred Heart University’s Computer Science Education (110) Certificate program is designed to provide teachers who hold a valid Connecticut teaching certificate with an additional endorsement to teach computer science in grades K-12. The curriculum aligns with the Connecticut State Department of Education (CSDE) standards for computer science education and prepares candidates to pass the Praxis II Computer Science (5008) exam. The program is offered fully online, allowing educators flexibility to pursue their professional development while maintaining their current teaching responsibilities.

column2: Cybersecurity Certificate
column47: The Cybersecurity Certificate is a 15-credit program designed for working professionals who desire to gain essential knowledge and hands-on skills in cybersecurity. This program can be completed in as little as 10 months and is offered both on campus and online. The program is ideal for individuals with a bachelor’s degree in IT, computer science, or a related field, as well as professionals who want to transition into the cybersecurity industry. Upon successful completion of the certificate program, students can pursue an advanced degree such as a Master of Science in Cybersecurity, which would require an additional 15 credits. The curriculum addresses key areas, including an introduction to cybersecurity, network security, ethical hacking and penetration testing, security architecture, and cryptography. The courses are developed using the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education (NICE) framework, which defines the cybersecurity workforce. As such, students will be well-prepared to take industry certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CySA+, PenTest+, EC-Council CEH, and Cisco CCNA Cyber Ops. Graduates from the program will be qualified to fill positions such as cybersecurity analyst, network security engineer, information security officer, security consultant, ethical hacker, and penetration tester.

column47: The graduate-level Database Design Certificate program at Sacred Heart University is designed for working professionals seeking to gain the necessary knowledge and skills to develop, implement, manage, and use database systems within a business environment. The program will prepare students for a career as a data analyst, database administrator, or database developer. This program provides students with practical exposure to the conceptual, logical, and physical design of databases, data modeling, SQL, NoSQL, data warehousing, and data mining, along with current issues in database management systems.

column47:
Sacred Heart University’s Intermediate Administrator (092) Certification program offers a planned program of study for certified teachers, school psychologists, school social workers, school counselors, and speech language pathologists who aspire to become district or school administrators and leaders in today’s schools. The program provides a conceptual framework for leadership and administration based on the Connecticut Common Core of Teaching and the Intermediate Administrator Certification (092) requirements. The 092 program is a 30-credit planned program of study. Students who have previously earned a 092 certificate are required to apply for the 6th-year certificate, a 30-credit planned program of study for individuals who wish to work toward the 092 certificate.

Mission Statement
The mission of the Sacred Heart University Department of Educational Leadership is to develop and empower highly effective educational leaders who facilitate teaching and learning, are committed to diversity and social justice, promote ethical practice, and lead with compassion.

Program Learning Objectives
Upon completion of the Intermediate Administrator (092) Certification program, candidates will be able to:
*   Apply research-based knowledge regarding effective school leadership through the lens of social justice.
*   Synthesize knowledge of curriculum, instruction, and assessment needed for effective school leadership.
*   Identify the legal, ethical, and practical issues involved in managing school resources.
*   Develop skills needed to lead, engage, and collaborate with families and community members.
*   Evaluate how school leaders foster diversity, equity, and inclusion in schools.
*   Articulate an understanding of how to implement the Connecticut Code of Professional Responsibility for Educators in real-world settings.

column50: The Robert W. Plaster College of Business, which houses the Artificial Intelligence graduate certificate, is accredited by AACSB International.

column2: Post-BS Certificate in Patient Safety and Healthcare Quality
column16: Applicants to the Certificate in Patient Safety and Healthcare Quality must hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution and have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better. Students interested in pursuing the Certificate in Patient Safety and Healthcare Quality must apply through Sacred Heart University's Office of Graduate Admissions. In addition to the official graduate application, applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended. Two letters of recommendation. A current resume. A personal statement.
column47: The Post-BS Certificate in Patient Safety and Healthcare Quality provides an opportunity for healthcare professionals to enhance their knowledge and skills in key areas of patient safety and quality improvement. The curriculum is designed to meet the growing demand for healthcare professionals who can lead initiatives to improve the quality of care and reduce medical errors. The program integrates theoretical knowledge with practical application, preparing graduates to apply evidence-based strategies in diverse healthcare settings. This certificate also provides students with 15 graduate credits that can be applied to the Master of Science in Patient Safety and Healthcare Quality.

column2: Post-Master's Certificate in Superintendency and Educational System Administration
column16:
Applicants for the Post-Master’s Certificate in Superintendency and Educational System Administration must submit the following:
*   Official transcript from an accredited university indicating the award of a master’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   Official transcripts from all other institutions where college credit was earned.
*   Evidence of five years of successful teaching experience and two years of successful administrative experience, certified by the superintendent of schools or designee on school district letterhead.
*   Proof of Connecticut or comparable out-of-state administrator certification (092).
*   Current resume.
*   Two letters of recommendation from professional references who can attest to the applicant’s leadership potential and successful teaching and administrative experience.
*   A written statement of professional goals.
column38: Isabelle Farrington College of Education and Human Development
column47: This 15-credit Post-Master’s Certificate (PMC) in Superintendency and Educational System Administration is an approved State of Connecticut program for individuals who wish to pursue a leadership role in educational system administration (e.g., Assistant Superintendent, Superintendent). The 15-credit program can be completed in approximately one year. Candidates are required to hold a master’s degree from an accredited institution, plus an Intermediate Administrative/Supervisor (092) endorsement or its equivalent. The Post-Master’s Certificate (PMC) in Superintendency and Educational System Administration will prepare individuals to successfully lead a school district in meeting the challenges of the 21st century. The curriculum, course sequence, field experiences, and exit requirements for the PMC in Superintendency and Educational System Administration meet the competencies and standards as defined by the Connecticut State Department of Education (CSDE) and the National Council for the Accreditation of Teacher Education (NCATE) and will prepare candidates for 093 certification. In addition, the PMC program is designed to integrate the mission of Sacred Heart University by fostering an awareness of social justice through the course curriculum, field experiences, and interactions with practitioners.
column50: The curriculum, course sequence, field experiences, and exit requirements for the PMC in Superintendency and Educational System Administration meet the competencies and standards as defined by the Connecticut State Department of Education (CSDE) and the National Council for the Accreditation of Teacher Education (NCATE).

column2: Post-Master's Certificate in Reading Teacher Education
column16: Admission to the Post-Master’s Certificate in Reading Teacher Education requires an official transcript indicating successful completion of a master’s degree from an accredited institution. In addition, the following must be submitted with the application: Three letters of recommendation (at least two from academic sources). A personal statement that discusses the applicant’s background and experiences related to the field of reading and literacy. A valid Connecticut teaching certificate or equivalent. A resume detailing professional and academic experiences. An interview may be required.
column47: This certificate program is designed for certified teachers who hold a master's degree and wish to obtain a Connecticut teaching certificate as a Reading and Language Arts Consultant (102) and/or a Connecticut teaching certificate as a Remedial Reading and Remedial Language Arts (097). Candidates also receive training in the administration and supervision of reading programs. This program is a 24-credit graduate level program. It does not lead to an additional master's degree but fulfills the academic requirements for the Connecticut certification.
column50: Approved by the Connecticut State Department of Education.

column2: Web Development Graduate Certificate
column16: Applicants to the Graduate Certificate in Web Development must possess an earned baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Strong academic performance is expected, with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 required for admission. Applicants are required to submit: 1. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. 2. Three letters of recommendation (professional or academic). 3. Resume. 4. Personal statement.
column47: The Web Development Graduate Certificate provides students with the fundamental concepts, theories, and skills in web development, ranging from client-side programming to back-end technologies. Students learn how to create and maintain interactive web pages, web applications, and web services. Students completing the Certificate will be able to develop interactive web applications and services.

column2: Certificate in Computer Science Education Endorsement
column16: To be considered for admission to the Computer Science Education Endorsement program, applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution and a valid teaching certificate. All applicants must submit the following: A completed online application, Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework, Copy of valid teaching certificate, Two letters of recommendation (professional or academic), A current resume, A personal statement, Official GRE scores (if undergraduate GPA is below a 3.0)
column38: Isabelle C. and William J. Lepper School of Computer Science and Engineering
column47:
As the world becomes more technology-driven, the demand for computer science education in K-12 schools continues to rise. Sacred Heart University’s Computer Science Education Endorsement program will prepare you to teach foundational computer science concepts to students in elementary, middle, and high school. This 15-credit program provides educators with the knowledge and skills necessary to teach computer science effectively, meeting the growing need for qualified computer science teachers.
Through engaging coursework and practical experiences, you will explore topics such as computational thinking, programming, data analysis, cybersecurity, and the societal impacts of computing. Our curriculum aligns with the Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA) K-12 Computer Science Standards and the International Society for Technology in Education (ISTE) Standards for Educators.
Upon completion of the program, you will be eligible for the Connecticut Department of Education (CS 105) Computer Science Endorsement, allowing you to teach computer science in Connecticut public schools. Join us at Sacred Heart University and become a leader in computer science education, shaping the next generation of innovators and problem-solvers.
